Nick Wagoner Nov 27, 2026, 06:03 PM ET

SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy (ankle) will not play on Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks, according to coach Kyle Shanahan.

After the Niners wrapped up their third and final session of the week, Shanahan said Purdy has officially been ruled out against the Seahawks. Mac Jones will start in Purdy's place with Kurtis Rourke as his backup.

"Anytime it's not a high ankle sprain, you get pretty relieved, but it was more mid than low, which is a little bit worse," Shanahan said. "Kind of had a feeling just the way it was by the time Wednesday came around. [It] didn't heal up as fast as we wanted, so had to shut him down."

Purdy initially injured his left ankle in the second quarter of last week's win against the Minnesota Vikings. The injury appeared to happen with about 30 seconds left in the opening half when Purdy tried to escape Vikings defensive lineman Jalen Redmond.

As a flag for intentional grounding came out, Purdy's left ankle appeared to bend under Redmond as he took him to the ground. Shanahan said Wednesday that he knew about Purdy's injury at halftime and it did not affect the way his play calling over the final two quarters.

After initially expressing optimism that Purdy would be OK to play the Seahawks, Shanahan said the injury simply didn't improve enough during the week to play. Shanahan said surgery is not necessary for Purdy and the hope is he can return for Week 13 against the New York Giants.

"It's too soon [to tell] but I'm pretty optimistic about it," Shanahan said. "But I was about this week to start and then it changes. So, hopefully it'll be all right."

Jones started eight games in Purdy's stead in 2025 when Purdy dealt with a turf toe injury.
